title: Spectrum Is Not Enough: A Random-Matrix Account of Data-Free Preconditioning for Differentially Private Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.21312v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Data-free preconditioning builds the Kronecker factors of KFAC from synthetic probes instead of private data. DP-KFC validates a probe by matching the eigenvalue decay of the private factors; we turn this criterion into a random-matrix account of what a probe can reconstruct. A single dichotomy organizes it: in the factorization $ A \otimes G $, the error-signal factor $ G $ and the architecture-determined bulk of the activation factor $ A $ are reconstructible without data, while only the data-induced spikes of $ A $ are not. We prove the $ G $ half is data-insensitive up to an explicit error-energy bound, with zero violations over a full training trajectory across four modalities and a natural-image benchmark. We locate the failure boundary at a Baik-Ben Arous-P\'ech\'e threshold: a bulk-only probe suffers an exact damage $s^2/(1-s^2)$ from a data-induced spike, which becomes invisible once it exceeds $(d/n)^{1/4}$, confirmed on an inj

translated_title: 谱信息并不足够：差分隐私学习中无数据预条件化的随机矩阵分析
translated_abstract: 无数据预条件化通过合成探针而非私有数据来构建 KFAC 的 Kronecker 因子。DP-KFC 通过匹配私有因子的特征值衰减来验证探针的有效性；我们将这一准则转化为一个关于探针究竟能够重构什么内容的随机矩阵理论框架。整个分析由一个单一的二分法组织：在分解 $A \otimes G$ 中，误差信号因子 $G$ 以及激活因子 $A$ 中由网络架构决定的主体部分无需数据即可重构，而唯一不可重构的是 $A$ 中由数据引起的特征值尖峰。我们证明了 $G$ 这一半对数据不敏感，其误差不超过一个显式的误差能量界，且在四种模态和一个自然图像基准的完整训练轨迹上实现了零违反。我们将失效边界定位在 Baik-Ben Arous-Péché 阈值处：仅含主体部分的探针会因数据引起的尖峰而遭受精确为 $s^2/(1-s^2)$ 的损伤，而一旦尖峰超过 $(d/n)^{1/4}$，该损伤便变得不可见，这一结论在注入……（摘要截断处）上得到验证。
tldr: 该论文用随机矩阵理论刻画了差分隐私学习中无数据 K-FAC 预条件化的可重构性，证明了 Kronecker 分解 $A \otimes G$ 中的误差因子 $G$ 和激活因子 $A$ 的架构决定部分可由合成探针在无数据情况下重构，只有 $A$ 中由数据引起的特征值尖峰不可重构，并精确定位了其在 Baik-Ben Arous-Péché 阈值 $(d/n)^{1/4}$ 处的失效边界。
en_tdlr: This paper provides a random-matrix account of data-free K-FAC preconditioning for differentially private learning, proving that in the decomposition $A \otimes G$, the error-signal factor $G$ and the architecture-determined bulk of the activation factor $A$ are reconstructible from synthetic probes without data, while only data-induced spikes of $A$ are not, with the failure boundary precisely located at a Baik-Ben Arous-Péché threshold of $(d/n)^{1/4}$.
